question.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\int \csc x \cot x \, \textrm dx = - \csc x + C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =-\int (\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+C \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
